attributes.description: The newest 200 events of the audit stream after the noise gate (health pings, query internals, API key lookups and page-load lookups, this suite reading itself and its own automated install, and bulk authentication removed), and without Kibana’s own routine API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account, every few seconds; Command Center’s Privileged ops tile counts it): the firehose you can actually read. Detail is the Kibana message (body.text), the transport action on an Elasticsearch event, which carries no message, or for a security configuration change what it changed (“API key <name or id> + N more” when one call invalidated several keys, “role <name>”). Client IP reads none recorded on an event with no client address, such as Kibana’s service account working inside the platform. Outcome reads attempted where Kibana logged an attempt rather than a result. Client IP is the forwarded public address; one marked internal (100.64.x, 10.x and other private ranges) is Kibana or the platform calling Elasticsearch on a person’s behalf, not where the person is. Open in Discover to page further back, add the object type or country, or filter on a cell. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.
